units: <cite ref="Habakkuk 2:19">Hab. II, 19</cite> <cite ref="D00237"><he>דַּמְיָא</he></cite> (some ed. incorr. <cite ref="T00001"><he>ר׳</he></cite>).

senses.gloss: to imagine, suspect, consider, Targ. I Kings VIII, 27 דָּמֵי (incorr. חמי).—Part. act. a. pass. דָּמֵי suspected, considered; resembling, like.—
units: Yeb. 114ᵇ אמרה בדְדָמֵי she speaks of what was to be suspected (under the circumstances, though she has not seen it).—שפיר דמי it is considered as right, it is right.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 38b:4">Ab. Zar. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ ד׳</he> it is all right (is permitted).
<cite ref="Berakhot 13b:23">Ber. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>הא מיגנא ש׳ ד׳</he> but to lie (on the back) is permitted; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 25b:25">Ber. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>כוליה ביתא … ד׳</he> the entire house is to be considered (for legal purposes) as four cubits.

Ib. 4ᵇ כתפלה אריכתא דַמְיָא is to be considered as one continued prayer, v. אֲרִיכָא; a. fr.—היכי דמי (abbrev. ה״ד) what is it like? in what case? Yeb. 63ᵇ ה״ד אשה רעה what do you call ‘a bad wife’? Sabb. 4ᵃ ה״ר אילימא וכ׳ what case do you mean? Do you mean the case of an involuntary transgressor &c.?; a. v. fr.—
Targ. Y. I Deut. XXXII, 32, v. Pa.—
<cite ref="Eruvin 54a:22">Erub. 54ᵃ</cite> <he>כהלולא ד׳</he> is like a wedding feast (soon passing away).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 85a:9">B. Kam. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>דַּמְיַת עלי כאריא וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A02950"><he>אֲרַב</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Taanit 21b:10">Taan. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>דַּמְיָין מעייהו ל־</he> their entrails look like those of human beings; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 14b:11">Pes. 14ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מי דָמֵי</he> is this like (the other)?, i.e. there is no analogy between them.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 40:25">Targ. Is. XL, 25</cite>; a. fr.—
Ḥull. 55ᵇ, a. e. טרפות קא מְדַמְּיַת להדדי you compare cases of T’refoth to one another (form an analogy)? (v. preced. Pi.).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 47a:18">Snh. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>מי קא מדמית וכ׳</he> can you compare &c.?—Part. pass. <he>מְדַמֵּי</he>, f. <cite ref="M00308"><he>מְדַמְיָא</he></cite>, pl. <he>מְדַמְיָין</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Deuteronomy 32:32">Targ. Y. II, Deut. XXXII, 32</cite> sq. (Y. I <he>דמי׳</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 11:23">Targ. Jud. XI, 23</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 45:9">Targ. Is. XLV, 9</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be like, to take an example.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 6:6">Targ. Prov. VI, 6</cite> <he>אִתְדְּמֵא וכ׳</he> imitate the ant (ed. Vien. <cite ref="T00809"><he>אִתְרְמֵי</he></cite>, read <he>אתד׳</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 102:7">Targ. Ps. CII, 7</cite>; a. e.—Y. Shek. IV, 48ᵈ top; Y. Dem. I, 21ᵈ bot. <he>לא אִידְּמִינָן</he> we cannot compare ourselves.
<cite ref="Gittin 57b:2">Gitt. 57ᵇ</cite> <he>אייתו דמי ולא אִידְּמוּ</he> they brought blood of animals but it did not look like (the blood of the prophet); a. fr.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 81a:3">Kidd. 81ᵃ</cite> … <he>אי׳ ליה שטן כ</he> Satan appeared to him as a woman &c.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 29b:2">Ib. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>אי׳ ליה וכ׳</he> (a demon) appeared to him as a monster &c.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 95a:2">Snh. 95ᵃ</cite> <cite ref="D00792"><he>אד׳</he></cite>; a. fr.
